title: Localizations of the integers are fields or discrete valuation rings
statement: The ring $\mathbf Z$ is a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] Dedekind domain (that is, a Noetherian integrally closed domain of Krull dimension one, in the sense of Stacks Tags 034W and 034X) with fraction field $\mathbf Q$. Its prime ideals are $(0)$ and the ideals $(p)$ generated by rational primes $p$. The localization $\mathbf Z_{(0)}$ is the field $\mathbf Q$, and for every nonzero prime ideal $(p)$ the localization $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local discrete valuation ring (that is, a Noetherian local domain of Krull dimension one whose maximal ideal is principal, as characterized by [lem-sc-normal-dim1-dvr] and Stacks Tag 00PD) with maximal ideal $(p)\mathbf Z_{(p)}$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 034X (lemma-characterize-Dedekind), implication (1) => (2), together with Definition Tag 034W and Lemma Tag 0AUQ (a PID is Dedekind); the description of prime ideals of $\mathbf Z$ and $\mathbf Z_{(0)}=\mathbf Q$ is the elementary PID calculation used in the same lemma. The characterization of a Noetherian one-dimensional local domain as a DVR is Lemma Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr).

mathlib_searches.query: prime ideals of the integer ring Z and localization at a nonzero prime is a discrete valuation ring
mathlib_searches.results: No declaration packages the arithmetic fact that Z is Dedekind or that its nonzero prime localizations are DVRs; Mathlib exposes generic localization and ideal APIs only
No matching declaration for Dedekind domains or discrete valuation rings; generic Localization.AtPrime and Ideal.IsPrime declarations only
No theorem asserting that ℤ is Dedekind or that its localizations are DVRs; only generic localization, valuation, and ideal infrastructure
